rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived KnowledgeSurplusLowDebtValue (identical structure, merely dropping `dltt` from the debt term), and the short-term-debt leg is already covered by RDLongHorizonFinancingValue, so it adds no new mechanism.

The expression matches the hypothesis and the own-history rank of R&D-adjusted ROA is a genuinely different conditioner from the archived volatility- and revenue-productivity-based variants, though the incremental economic content over PeakKnowledgeProductivityValue is modest.

Because the five-year R&D stock is several times current R&D, `LAG(TS_SUM(xrd,5),1) - xrd` is numerically dominated by the R&D-capital level, so the signal is effectively R&D-capital intensity interacted with pre-R&D earnings yield (already tested in ReportedYieldHiddenCapitalResilience) rather than the claimed "harvesting phase" indicator.

Structurally this is ReportedYieldHiddenCapitalResilience with one interaction leg swapped from cross-sectional to time-series rank of the same earnings yield — a defensible but largely cosmetic modification of an already-evaluated, mediocre signal.

Using gross profit rather than net income as the coverage base for persistent R&D is a coherent and materially different affordability measure from the archived SustainableInnovationValue, and the multiplicative form and sign are internally consistent, though it remains an incremental refinement of a previously weak family.

This simply bolts together the conditioning legs of two already-tested archive signals (PeakKnowledgeProductivityValue's peak-productivity term and RDLongHorizonFinancingValue's short-debt term) onto the same pre-R&D earnings yield, which is a high-overfitting-risk recombination rather than a new mechanism.
